Instrument map on the real device: descriptor full-set rebuild 9.14 ms/frame (35%, 445 rebuilds/frame at ~20.6 us vs ~3 us for a memo hit), snapshot 4.59 ms (12.4 MB/frame), guest 'other' 4.57 ms (2664 guest ops/frame), vkCmdDraw 3.13 ms (683 draws), cleanup 1.82 ms (writebacks 1.05 with 9.6 MB/frame, destroying 668 buffer views 0.51). Two new facts: with the memo on, the slot set_cache is bypassed entirely (hits=0.0), and every texel binding gets a fresh target buffer each frame so the buffer-view cache never hits. All 43 ab_off path switches swept (previous rounds only swept the 29 live-set booleans): no free gains; only passfast (off costs -3.34 fps) and texelcopy (off costs -2.77 fps) beat the scan bias, both in the helping direction. Probe (branch task/T-mavis-perf-20261122-v2probe, commit 2123237, ~200 lines): a per-slot pooled texel destination whose buffer identity never changes, refreshed on every use through the same per-submission copy cache as before, so a texel binding can join the descriptor memo. Measured on the device with an interleaved A/B: texelpool=1 fps median 27.55 / submit_cpu 31.10 ms vs texelpool=0 fps median 28.57 / submit_cpu 28.61 ms, i.e. dfps -1.02 and dcpu +2.49 ms/frame, rejected under L-029. Attribution: rebuilds fell only 445 -> 342 (-1.62 ms/frame) while the hit path now refreshes 1629 times/frame at 1.69 us (+2.75 ms/frame). tasks.checkpoint: Version 2 SHIPPED under L-029 (gain +38%, far above the +-3.5 fps noise). Root cause found: the engine graphics worker dm-gfx is the ONLY thread in the process whose Cpus_allowed_list is 0-6 (every other one of the 40+ threads is 0-7) - the system narrows it out of the Cortex-X4 (cpu7, 3.014 GHz) a few seconds into the heavy scene, leaving it on the Cortex-A720 cores (cpu3-6, 2.803 GHz). The same workload (draws=602, ops/draws unchanged) then costs submit_cpu_ms 15.4 -> 24.9-27.2 and fps 45.9 -> 33.3. This finally explains the old mystery of "the frame rate drops from 40+ to 26-30 about 20 s after reaching the position and stays there": the drop IS the moment the mask is narrowed. Ruled out with evidence: thermal throttling (Thermal Status 0, battery 21 C, CPU zones 52-65 C), other processes pre-empting the CPU, the cgroup (the process is in cpuset:/vip but every other thread there is 0-7), this repository (no sched_setaffinity anywhere in src/) and the guest (its import resolution is a strict allowlist, so it cannot even reach sched_setaffinity, and nn::os::SetThreadCoreMask is bound to an empty HLE stub). Thread-level sampling also showed the earlier L-067 attribution to the main thread was wrong and it is withdrawn (L-069): ffrs.gamewindow only uses ~5% of a core while dm-gfx uses 90-100% of one. Fix: the worker pins itself to the fastest core detected from cpufreq at start and re-checks the mask every frame, taking it back if the system narrows it again; a heterogeneity gate keeps homogeneous devices on the system scheduler, and a failed sched_setaffinity falls back to the system placement. Rendering path untouched: the diff is 1 rewritten line plus 152 added lines, no draw, fence, pacing, texture or shader change. Measured in-process interleaved A/B in the foundry deep area with the engine accumulating per arm (windows never straddle an arm): big arm (mask 0x78, cpu3-6 A720) fps 33.2-34.4 with submit_cpu_ms 24.3-25.8, prime arm (mask 0x80, cpu7 X4) fps 43.3-48.5 with submit_cpu_ms 15.5-16.2. tasks.checkpoint: Diagnostic round, NO version shipped (nothing measured above the noise). Per-frame facts in the fire scene with the shipped build: 516.2 set builds per frame of which 493.4 are excluded by the texel rule (UNIFORM_TEXEL_BUFFER, excluded because texel_memo_enabled is false in the shipped build), 14.9 storage-image, 6.0 storage-write, 0.9 dynbuf-reject; the descriptor memo serves 353.5 hits per frame with 0.6-1.1 misses; the slot-local set cache serves 0.0 because it is fully bypassed (fresh_skips 119.0 + experiment_skips 397.6 = all 516). The descriptor build is 6.72 ms/frame un-instrumented (~47% of submit_cpu 14.4 ms), and the engine's own 21-part descriptor timing (obtained without rebuilding, via the gfx-cpu-profile entry point) splits it as image_lookup 29%, element_rest 16%, set_finalize 15%, buffer_bind 9%, remaining 11%, texel_* 13%. THREE findings change the plan. (1) The previous round's prerequisite is WITHDRAWN: V3 claimed the memo key changes every frame, but the keydiff census never produces data in this build - it only runs on a true lookup miss, and there are none (the 0.9 misses/frame equal the why[3]=dynbuf rejection count while all six rejection counters vwhy=blk/buf/ord/img/tex/stor are 0). The key is not the blocker; V3's net loss came from the pooling and hit-path overhead. (2) Three runtime experiments via live-set in one session (fire scene, draws~735, 5 samples per arm) put a price on the memo: baseline fps 54.2-56.9 with submit_cpu 14.2-14.7; texelframe=1 changes nothing (that branch is unreachable while texel_memo_enabled is false - a useful control); descmemo=0 gives fps 53.8-55.7 with submit_cpu 15.3-15.4, so the whole descriptor memo is worth only about 0.9 ms/frame, and it exposes the slot-local set cache hitting 367/frame (normally masked, because desc_memo_enabled forces experiment_cache_skip regardless of the honorsetbypass switch) - and that set cache is the cheaper mechanism by ~0.9 ms/frame. (3) Both arms show nearly the same template-update count (516 vs 505), because the set cache sits inside descriptors_build and only saves the set allocation plus the template update, not the per-binding work: the real cost driver is the 493 texel draws themselves, which neither mechanism can cover because their key holds a per-slot texel view. The texel path was measured too: 401 texel-pending calls per frame, 8.57 MB per frame of full copies, 9.32 MB per frame of allocation, 0.55 MB per frame of CPU-side copies. Next-round hypothesis, now precise: give the texel binding a view that survives the slot (persistent resident buffer refreshed by dirty ranges) so the set key becomes stable, and the already-proven 367-hits-per-frame set cache can then cover those draws, worth up to ~6.7 ms/frame of rebuild work (fire scene 55 fps towards the 60 Hz cap) while turning the 8.57 MB/frame full copy into a dirty-range copy. Pre-check that can kill it in one run: how many texel bytes actually change per frame (the engine already has the counters, but write tracking reports dirty_pages_per_frame=0.0 in this scene, so dirty-range tracking has to be enabled first). tasks.checkpoint: Diagnostic round, NO version shipped (the measured net is negative, so L-029 stops the build cycle). Three findings. (1) The round-6 section 14.4 figures are INSTRUMENTATION ARTIFACTS and are corrected: the 8.57 MB/frame of texel full copies and the 9.32 MB/frame of allocation were taken inside a gfx-cpu-profile window, where instrumentation sets normal=false, the texel_copy_cache cacheable gate fails and the copy cache is bypassed (the tell is that NVN PERF texelcopy normal=0 is all zeros). The real normal-session figures in the same fire scene (draws~735) are texel 1.75 MB/frame with only 3 real copies of 400 KB per frame (the rest are frame-internal reuse hits) and VERTEX 3.84-4.03 MB/frame, i.e. vertex is the copy volume, not texel. Therefore the round-6 estimate that dirty-range refresh would remove 8.57 MB/frame of copies does not hold. (2) The prerequisite (how many texel bytes change per frame) is answered from the engine own counters, without rebuilding: gfx-live-set texmemo=1 opens the cross-frame resident path (texel_acquire, content-hash based) and reports texel_hits (content unchanged, copy reused) against texel_refreshes (content changed, copy required). Measured in the fire scene: hits 761-776/frame, refreshes 126.6-127.0/frame, so about 84 percent of texel reads are content-stable; texel_binds 257/frame, distinct 173, reused 2.0, fallback 17-21, evict 17-22. The premise for dirty-range refresh HOLDS, but its payoff is capped because the texel copy volume was never large (see 1). (3) The mechanism itself works and is correctly invalidated, but the NET is negative: with texmemo=1 the set builds per frame drop 516 -> 264 (-49 percent), the texel memo exclusion drops 493 -> ~200/frame, the descriptor build drops 10.44-10.50 ms -> 5.60 ms (-4.9 ms) and the texel snapshot bytes drop 1.75 MB -> 0.04 MB, while the memo hit path pays for it: descriptor domain 9.14 -> 6.82-6.93 ms (only -2.2 to -2.3 ms net), hash domain 0.08 -> 0.29-0.30 ms, hit_total 0.64 -> 2.88-2.90 ms. Summed over all CPU domains (fire-scene same-scope, medians; 352 samples on arm vs 844 off) the net is -1.95 ms/frame, i.e. FASTER: descriptor 8.92 -> 6.95 ms, hash 0.08 -> 0.29 ms, snapshot 2.62 -> 2.27 ms, build 10.28 -> 5.58 ms, hit_total 0.62 -> 2.86 ms, domain sum 17.13 -> 15.18 ms. tasks.checkpoint: Diagnostic round, NO version shipped. The round-8 entry point was to stop hunting for 1 ms on the CPU side and look at the GPU, which no round had ever measured. Using the engine's own runtime marker gfx-pass-live (one-shot, per-frame GPU pass and compute timestamps, no rebuild) the fire scene's GPU side was measured for the first time. (1) Baseline: the internal render resolution is 768x436 (71 of 96 passes), not the display coordinate space; the fire scene runs 96 render passes, 735 draws and 135 dispatches per frame. One frame's GPU budget: pass 9.86 ms + compute 3.18 ms + a 2.13 ms gap that belongs to no pass and no dispatch = 15.07 ms, matching the 14.7-15.1 ms submission span. The top four passes hold 53 percent of the pass time, and the same geometry is rasterized twice per frame (585504 and 585642 vertices, 242 and 246 draws, once into 7 attachments at 2366 us and once into 1 attachment at 749 us), together 32 percent of GPU pass time; the fixed per-pass overhead baseline is about 23 us (40 post-process passes share one shader pair and cost 23-31 us each), so 96 passes cost roughly 2.2 ms/frame of pure pass overhead. (2) Two outlier passes were isolated: i=13 at 600/602/608 us and i=17 at 422/422/429 us, against 63 us for a structurally identical pass, and 600 vs 210 us for two passes with the same shader pair, so the cost is in what the fragment shader reads or in the attachment load/store, not in the pass structure; not yet attributed. (3) The core finding is that span_us is defined as the first record's q0 to the last record's q1, so span minus pass minus compute is the GPU time between all render passes and compute dispatches. It scales with the compute burst in a slot (1 dispatch gives 0 us, 3 gives 2 us, 15 gives 96 us, 115 gives 2011-2032 us across five frames with a spread of 21 us) and is independent of that slot's compute volume. (4) Decisive exclusion of the obvious alternative: the natural explanation is that the GPU catches up with the CPU and idles, since the CPU is the bottleneck. An interleaved A/B with descmemo=0 added 1.28 ms of submit_cpu and cost 3.6 fps, and the gap did not move at all (2028 / 2022 / 2032 / 2031 us), so this is real GPU work (L-095). (5) Attribution to the storage writeback path, from three independent pieces of evidence: the engine's own READBACK_TIMING shows alloc_bytes of 9.32 MB/frame over 430 readback allocations per frame while CPU copies into them are only 0.78 MB/frame, so roughly 8.5 MB/frame is written by the GPU; the readback arena is allocated HOST_VISIBLE | HOST_COHERENT | HOST_CACHED, so the GPU writes results straight into host-visible memory; and the bandwidth cross-check gives 9.32 MB / 2.0 ms = 4.66 GB/s for the GPU write against 11 GB/s for a CPU memcpy of the same bytes, so the GPU write to host-visible memory is 2.4x slower than a CPU memcpy (L-096). The cleanup counter adds a CPU-side host-to-host memcpy of 7.1 MB/frame (0.64 ms when idle, 2.58 ms when loaded). Together this is 2.6-4.6 ms/frame, 12-20 percent of the frame, and it is the first sizeable target in nine rounds that does not depend on a duplicate gain. (6) Three candidate fixes are scoped in section 17.6, none of which change rendering: (A) make the writeback destination device-local and add one device-to-host copy at retire (GPU side 2.0 to about 0.9 ms estimated); (B) make the writeback lazy so the copy happens when the guest actually reads the range; (C) allocate the guest storage buffers HOST_VISIBLE so the CPU-side host-to-host memcpy disappears, though the 2.0 ms GPU write remains. Option A is the smallest bounded change but must preserve the pending-view semantics byte for byte (L-032). (7) Side confirmation: occlusion queries are already in the batched mode at 155.7 per frame, not the 2200 per draw that an engine comment records as costing the Adreno 730 about 10 ms of GPU time, so that old lead needs no further work; per frame there are also 448.9 barriers from compute dispatches whose destination stage mask still contains ALL_GRAPHICS and ALL_COMMANDS, and whether those can be deferred to the end of the compute run is the alternative explanation for the gap that is not yet fully separated from the writeback copy. Why no version: the change lands on the writeback correctness path (L-032) and the device was thermally loaded, so a trustworthy display regression (90 frames, 10 segments of 9 consecutive presented frames) was not possible; L-029 stops the build cycle. Experience entries L-094..L-096.

Round 25 acceptance: the img-persistence direction is closed with a same-session A/B (miss 225.3->0.0 per frame, fps median unchanged within 0.06 fps) and is not shipped; the two V20 changes are semantically equivalent, switchable at runtime and measured in one process with an A->B->A->B design; because the measured gain is below the noise floor (delta median +0.075 fps, opposite signs in the two pairs) no version ships this round (L-029); the snapshot slow path is attributed for the first time (pending_view 0.192 ms/frame, cpu_access 0.679 ms/frame, remainder 0.506 ms/frame), and the round-24 attribution that cpu_access is free in the snapshot path is explicitly retracted in the report.

Round 26 acceptance: a version ships because the same-session A->B->A->B design gives a delta above the noise floor with the same sign in both pairs (delta median +0.470 fps, +0.34 and +0.48 per pair), the display regression passes against a same-state drift baseline (ON-vs-OFF frame difference 1.729 mean / 12.65 percent of pixels above 2, versus the OFF-vs-OFF baseline 1.728 / 12.62 percent), and the skipped call is provably a no-op when the writeback interval index reports no overlap, with the index cross-checked against the linear scan by the engine own verify mode (486894 queries, zero mismatches and zero rebuild mismatches).

Round 27 acceptance: the round changed no code, built no package and left the device build untouched; it took one 60-frame CPU_TIMING window plus the engine built-in DESC_TIMING detail on the shipped version 4 (V21) in the arsenal scene and produced a full component-level attribution (descriptor 7.925 ms/frame, cleanup 1.669 ms/frame over 9.2 calls, draw 1.492, snapshot 0.846, dispatch 0.442, accounted exclusive total 14.13 ms/frame of a 25.74 ms measured frame) plus a descriptor-domain split (image_lookup 2.149, set_finalize 0.963, element_rest 0.959, buffer_bind 0.626, texel_view_create 0.356, texel_pending 0.345, texel_view_lookup 0.175, memo_key/snapshot/verify 0.489, remaining 0.724) whose counts reconcile (element_rest 8617 = buffer 4600 + image 4017). The round corrects itself against an earlier conclusion: image_lookup is NOT a new candidate, because the V11 card round-23 analysis already priced it at about 2.18 ms/frame as a per-call fixed cost (8-field ImgKey construction and hashing) and rejected the miss direction by a two-arm differential, so the 2.149 ms/frame measured here is a reproduction and the item stays closed. The round also records a new structural reading of the 442.9 descriptor-set rebuilds per frame: there are two independent causes, the set key embeds the VkBufferView handle while Slot::texel_views is destroyed and cleared at retire_slot (xbg_game.cpp:1871) so the handle necessarily changes, and s.set_cache.clear() at retire_slot (xbg_game.cpp:1876) empties the cache per recording session, so fixing only one cause cannot produce a single hit; a cross-frame cache therefore needs both changes plus invalidation hooks, which sits inside the L-032 red line, so no code was touched and nothing shipped.

Round 27b acceptance: the round changed no engine code and shipped no new binary; it brought up the engine on BOTH devices (the Honor and, for the first time from this session, the RG477M) and produced the dual-device effect regression - both devices render the full effect set (Honor V21: lava glow, steam columns, purple character aura, orange crystal flames, floating motes, volumetric light, blue lightning auras in battle; RG477M baseline 1.0.78-test: blue and pink particle fields, water reflections, waterfalls, lily pads, cave fire) with no missing effect observed; it identified the silent no-start root cause (the diagnostic Activity needs an explicit game_dir, otherwise resolveGameDir returns null and the guest never starts, with no log line at all); it attempted the strict same-camera pixel comparison against the pre-optimization baseline 1.0.73 on the Honor and reported it as NOT conclusive because the two builds did not share a camera position (best of 25 cross-matched pairs still mean|d| 18.54, and the largest deltas are the same fire drawn at a different screen position, not a missing layer), with the same-build frame drift baselines measured as the reason (1.0.73 median 2.41 versus V21 median 20.27); it archived the stable release with a verified sha256 and left the device install matching it, restored the Honor to the shipped V21 build, and left the RG477M package untouched with the temporarily copied save removed.

HONOR-SAVE-20261112: the save file lives in external app specific storage and survives APK updates, but the guest only flushes at its own save points, so installing a package while playing loses the progress since the last save point. HONOR-BATTLE-EFFECT-STUTTER (attribution withdrawn and re-scoped 2026-11-12): the device data refutes the original claim. Synchronous pipeline creation is NOT the cause of the >100 ms spikes (the largest single creation in the whole session is 1.3 ms). The cause is the CPU blocking in the submit path while the GPU is idle, marked by the readback/writeback drains (sync_rb 9.80 vs 0.03 per window). The repair point is the drain scheduling, which is task HONOR-TRANSIT-RETIRE-20261112. The warm list flush defect (Class A) is fixed; the seed is unproven and is being narrowed. The cold-start 4.5-4.8 s frame is still unexplained.

RG477M-TEXEL-FORMAT-20261112: on the RG477M (Mali-G615) the guest dies after about five seconds with FATAL: Texel format lacks formatless-write support. Mali reports bufferFeatures=0x78 for the texel formats, so the optional STORAGE_WRITE_WITHOUT_FORMAT and READ_WITHOUT_FORMAT bits are absent for the whole family. The typed path is available (0x78 contains STORAGE_TEXEL_BUFFER_BIT), so the fix is a SPIR-V rewrite. The game cannot be played on the handheld until this lands, which outranks the stutter. spirv-val (SPIRV-Tools v2026.4) passes all six translated shaders against the default SPIR-V target environment, and four of six against vulkan1.1 and against vulkan1.3. The two that fail are compute shaders that write to a storage image without a declared format and report 'Capability StorageImageWriteWithoutFormat is required to write to storage image'. The commands, the exit codes and the full output are in .local/shader-verify/val/.

The reference tree's game profile 0100606026F12000 is this game: its game.tsv names FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE, Unreal Engine 5.6.1, SDK 20.5.17, and its shader map holds the shader 174293a30c315aed with a key that matches this port byte for byte. Its conflict file states that there are no control section key conflicts, which this port measured independently over the whole shader set.

The sampler builder and texture builder families exist and are wired into the dispatch, the Android build and the contract build, so the contract and the device run compile the same sources. The contract case --nvn-builder covers both families: every name resolves and resolves to the same entry point, the values round trip, the defaults really reset, the device round trips, the guest's builder objects are not written, and the counters move. The three variant self proof is in git.

The command recording now has the record format of the same game reference. nvn_command_buffer.h and nvn_command_buffer.c write op_hdr{op,size} plus the payload struct, 47 of the 49 opcodes are written, and the opcode numbers match the reference tree one by one; JUMP and BEGIN are not written. nvn_command_buffer_opcode_name() resolves them. The host gate rebuild in .local/build-p-mm-28 exits 0.

A command buffer handle names an immutable package. nvn_command_package{handle,records,bytes,record_count} comes out of nvn_command_buffer_get_package(); recording the same buffer again, finalizing it or reusing the address does not overwrite the old package, and an unknown handle is refused. The contract case --nvn-command-buffer checks the opcode, that the payload holds the data rather than an address, and that the package does not change under the guest.

The data behind a pointer argument is copied during the call. The copied bytes counter counts every copy the call made, the payload copies included. A record that only named the address would be unreadable by the time the command runs, because the guest may write over its own memory the moment the call returns.

The guest's command memory callback runs through the guest's own thread. nvn_command_buffer_set_guest_call() is registered when the boundary is prepared in prepare_boundary_locked(), the call goes through nb_call_from_host on the boundary scope, a refused call is a failure with a named log line, and there is no raw fallback and no direct call to the pointer the guest handed over.

Sixteen entry points whose signature is not confirmed for this game are marked NVN_CB_ENTRY_DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY and the dispatch prints diagnostic recorder only for them, so they do not trap the guest, and the log tells the implemented names and the diagnostic ones apart.

All nine NVN families prove themselves in three variants on the new build .local/build-p-mm-28: the broken expectation with the gate kept is red, the same break with the gate removed and the error count hardcoded to zero is a false green that exits zero while its stdout still reports zero errors, and the untouched contract with a stub that lies is red. The scripts live in scripts/runtime/selfproof_nvn_*.sh with the variant generators next to them.

The guest crossed the sampler builder family on the device. The run of 2026-10-25 (APK sha256 1c8974cadce1842c19a72d3c8ab15fb7ee3f97b45ddd0b4afb755f549a942cee, transcript .local/logs/p-mm-29-guest-transcript.log with 58539 lines, a window of 300 seconds) shows the eight builder calls in order: SetDefaults, SetDevice, SetBorderColor, SetMinMagFilter, SetMaxAnisotropy, SetWrapMode, SetLodBias and SetLodClamp. The new first fatal is nvnSamplerInitialize, trap slot 71, caller lr 0x72130cfd3c, with the sampler object in x0 and the builder in x1.

The record format of this port is the record format of the reference tree, checked field by field by scripts/graphics/compare_nvn_record_format.py: the record header matches, all fifty opcodes match by name, by order and by number, and thirty-three payload structures have the same layout. The only difference is one member this port renamed, p_clear_buf's _pad is called pad here, which changes no layout. The report is under .local/shader-verify/record-format-comparison.json and the tool exits zero.

The guest's command memory callback does not reach the guest, and the reason is in the boundary's phase protocol and not in the recorder. nb_call needs the scope in its idle phase and nb_call_from_host needs it in its host phase, and the host phase only exists while a host function runs behind an import gateway. The NVN entry points are not import gateways, the guest calls the pointers nvnDeviceGetProcAddress handed out, so the scope is in its guest phase while they run and the boundary refuses both of its entries by design. The device run shows exactly that: status 4, which is NB_BUSY, three times, and then the recording is void. The thread check passed, so the caller is on the guest's own thread.

The reference that runs this game calls the callback directly and lends a segment of host memory when the guest cannot add enough, and it says why that is not an edge case for this game: the records are larger than the real device's NVN commands, so the budget the game reserved for real device usage runs out. The guest's own addresses are the host's addresses here, nso_base is the host image, so the callback pointer the guest hands over is already the host entry of the guest function, and nso_entry_address is what validates it against the module's text.

The device now asks for the feature the two compute shaders of this game need. The format of a storage image is a property of the bound texture and not of the shader, so there is nothing in the game's data to put into the module; the reference host that runs this game declares the capability and turns shaderStorageImageWriteWithoutFormat on in VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures. nvn_backend_vulkan.c queries the feature, asks for it only when the device supports it, and the log and the device description keep support and enablement apart. The device has not been asked whether it supports it yet.

The descriptor pools have their numbering bases again. A pool is given a base at its first Initialize and the numbering steps on by the pool's size rounded up to a whole number of 256, the way the reference host of this game does it, and the textures and the samplers have a numbering each. The base lives in its own table and survives the finalization of the pool, so a pool that is initialized again gets the same base back. The pools also answer which texture is registered at an index. Commit 83a64d5, host contract build p-mm-35 green.

The device supports shaderStorageImageWriteWithoutFormat. It was measured on the RG477M, with the support and the enablement kept apart, and the runtime's conditional enablement in nvn_backend_vulkan.c is therefore live on this handheld. P-MM-23, tier 1.

A compute pipeline whose module no longer declares the unused Float64 capability is created on the device and its dispatch is consumed: vkCreateComputePipelines returns VK_SUCCESS, vkQueueSubmit and vkWaitForFences both return VK_SUCCESS. The module that does declare it is rejected with VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED, which is what a device without shaderFloat64 does. P-MM-23, tiers 3 and 4.

vkCreateGraphicsPipelines crashes the Mali driver on the RG477M with SIGSEGV, and a control run whose vertex and fragment stages are hand written trivial shaders crashes at the same fault address. The crash is therefore in the graphics pipeline state and not in the game's shaders. P-MM-23, tier 3 not reached.

The guest's command memory callback is called on the guest thread with three explicit checks, and the host lends it a segment of memory when the guest cannot add enough, so a recording is never void. The host gate is green with 242 cases and the command memory family contract is at zero errors.

A handle is read with the numbering base of the pool that was bound: the command buffer keeps the base of the pool it bound in its own state, the single texture bind carries the bases in its record, and the replay adds them when it reads the handle. The contract makes two texture pools and checks that the number the replay read is the number in the pool plus the base the pool was given.

The capability declarations of a SPIR-V module can be corrected from the module itself: a capability the module uses is never dropped and the tool refuses instead. Measured on the six modules of this game with spirv-val --target-env vulkan1.1, the two compute modules fail before the correction and pass after it.

The 48 names the guest asks for between the sampler and its first draw are implemented and wired: the texture object family of 31 names, the texture view family of 14 names and the three device handle functions. They resolve through the guest own lookup, every name is stable and holds once, the texture keeps the values the builder had when it was initialized, the guest objects are not written, and the handle functions return the number inside the pool without the base of the pool. The host gate is green with 250 cases and both new family contracts are at zero errors.

The device limits the guest asks for are answered and the guest lives past the fatal of the empty texture id pool. On the device (the run of p-mm-43, the transcript .local/logs/p-mm-43-guest-transcript.log) the guest asked nvnDeviceGetInteger twenty three times and every answer came from the table: MAX_TEXTURE_POOL_SIZE 1048576, MAX_SAMPLER_POOL_SIZE 4096, MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE 16384 and the rest. The game got past its own NVNHelpers.cpp:240 and created memory pools, texture pools, sampler pools, textures, samplers, render states and blend states before it stopped.

The driver refuses the shaders of this game for two reasons, both measured on the device and neither of them the guess of P-MM-27: the three fragment modules declare the FragmentShaderPixelInterlockEXT capability and the SPV_EXT_fragment_shader_interlock extension, and the device has neither, so both have to be dropped; the vertex module declares Float64 and the device has no shaderFloat64, so that one word has to go. With the modules changed that way a graphics pipeline is built on the RG477M and a draw is consumed by the GPU.

The host side tables of the object families grow with the number of objects that are live. The contract asks for sixty four blend states, four times the size of the old table, and checks that all of them are there and still readable; against the old table of sixteen it fails with actual=0xf expected=0x40.

The presentation path of the device layer is a source of the host build and of the Android build now, so it is in the APK. Its contract passes with zero errors and its self proof measures the false green: variant B exits 0 while the log holds a real check failure.

The queue submission seam hands the command package of the handle the guest gives to the replay, and refuses an unknown handle by name. The worker measured a real race on the way: the replay resets a shared global state on every run, so two submissions at the same time corrupt each other; with the submission lock 0 of 30 runs failed and without it 12 of 12 did.

The guest does not abort any more. In the device run of p-mm-44 (the transcript .local/logs/p-mm-44-guest-transcript.log) there is no guest abort at all: the guest created its device, its queue with a real platform queue, seven memory pools, its sampler pool and its texture pool, made samplers, textures, texture views and programs, and kept running for eighty four seconds of its own clock before it stopped at nvnSyncInitialize.

The tables of the object families hold the objects of the game. In the same run no state was refused: the counts of 'no room for another' and 'the render state table is full' are both zero, where the run of p-mm-43 refused more than sixteen hundred blend states and more than four thousand render states.

The capability tool can remove an extension declaration, and two independent ways of removing the declarations agree: the output of scripts/graphics/fix_spirv_capabilities.py with --drop Float64 --drop FragmentShaderPixelInterlockEXT --drop-extension EXT_fragment_shader_interlock is byte for byte identical to the deliverable of P-MM-29, which was verified on the device, for all four modules of this game.

honor_render_root_cause.summary: The final presented game image carries alpha=0 for 92.1% of pixels while RGB holds the full picture. The blit into the swapchain preserves that alpha, and the swapchain is created with VK_COMPOSITE_ALPHA_INHERIT_BIT_KHR with no native window blending mode set, so the Honor compositor honours the alpha and multiplies the world away. Only the top-right mini-map/HUD has alpha!=0, so only it survives.

root_cause_chain.step_1: 63d3652 restores the GPU sync for indirect draws by letting cpu_access(why=5) call resolve_pending()
root_cause_chain.step_2: that sync only fires while the read still overlaps a pending writeback; the device log shows CPU_ACCESS_SYNC count 0 in the field scene
root_cause_chain.step_3: the device log shows 20 x NVN FIND_INDIRECT_FAIL with had_overlap=0 had_indirect=0, so the GPU-resident indirect template is already gone when the CPU needs it
root_cause_chain.step_4: d5a3340 removed the recent_indirect_batches fallback, the only remaining way to find an indirect batch whose writeback had already retired
root_cause_chain.step_5: refuted by experiment: gfx-wb-skip=0 leaves the flicker unchanged (moon region 82.9 <-> 103.4, std 9.80), so a dropped storage writeback is not the cause
root_cause_chain.step_6: confirmed by experiment: gfx-indexed-resident=1 enables the GPU-resident indirect template path (find_indirect_template); with it at 0 the path is disabled, the draw falls back to the CPU read with its GPU synchronization, and the user reports the moon is normal
root_cause_chain.step_7: the asymmetry behind it: current_pending_range, which hands out the GPU-resident view of the same range, requires w->slot==&slots[slot_index], but find_indirect_template accepted a template from any recording slot, so a template built from an earlier producer could be served and the draw used a stale instance count

moon_flicker_root_cause.key_finding_1: the draw sequence in the moon scene is strictly periodic with period 6 frames: period-6 match 99.7 percent on the raw per-draw trace and 93-98 percent on the production per-frame CSV, other tested periods (2,3,4,5,7,8) sit at 33-66 percent
moon_flicker_root_cause.key_finding_2: re-verified from the raw per-draw trace: the moon scene draw sequence is 79,79,80,80,79,79 repeating (period-6 match 99.7 percent, period-12 99.6 percent, other periods 33-66 percent); the earlier 80,80,81,80,81,81 phrasing came from the production CSV session and is the same structure with a different phase origin
moon_flicker_root_cause.key_finding_3: CORRECTED 2026-11-12: the phase-aligned 6-frame variation belongs to exactly ONE shader pair, vs=fae0b835a11360e2 / fs=4746d49d8e2bbaab, whose per-frame count is 11,11,12,12,11,11 (phases 2 and 3 carry one extra draw). An earlier note credited vs=17005546ca19abc9; the raw per-draw trace does not support that. Other pairs vary only on a separate non-phase-aligned event set (about 13.7 percent of frames: fs=4e81f73282ffd5b1 +1, fs=123f2ada0f802e0f -2, fs=b33659227a17c1a9 +1, fs=5a9fc0ecb88c6440 +1, net +1).
moon_flicker_root_cause.key_finding_4: the extra draw is INSERTED INSIDE the frame, not appended: on a phase-0 frame the target pair sits at ordinals 24,33,37,42,45,48,49,50,73,74,78; on a phase-2 frame at 24,25,34,38,43,46,49,50,51,74,75,79 (ordinal 25 is the extra one, everything after shifts by one).
moon_flicker_root_cause.key_finding_5: the production package reproduces the same 6-frame period as the diagnostic build, so the period is a property of the shipped rendering path, not of the diagnostic instrumentation
moon_flicker_root_cause.interpretation: 6 frames at 30 fps is 200 ms. A strictly per-phase, reproducible extra draw is a systematic synchronisation or scheduling artefact in the render path, not random game logic: game logic would not align unrelated shader pairs to one single phase.
moon_flicker_root_cause.not_yet_confirmed: STILL OPEN: the engine-side reason why the guest emits one extra halo draw on 2 of every 6 frames. The candidate is stale engine-published data (writeback slot lifetime / counter report) reaching the guest, or a frame-count-keyed engine state. A read-only per-draw parameter probe (marker gfx-draw-param-trace) is being built in the rescue worktree to compare the extra draw against its neighbours (same count/instances/ibuf = duplicated command; different parameters = a genuinely different batch).
moon_flicker_root_cause.correction_to_earlier_record: the earlier attribution in honor_moon_flicker_20261112 step_6/step_7 (the GPU-resident indirect template path) is NOT supported by this scene: in the moon scene all 344k+ traced indexed draws carry ind=0 and the device reports GPU indexed resident=0, so no indirect draw happens at all here. indirect_proof_enabled only gates find_indirect_template and indirect_template_batch. That attribution is downgraded to unconfirmed and must be re-tested.
moon_flicker_root_cause.refuted: gfx-wb-skip=0 leaves the flicker unchanged; gfx-bright reported bright applied=0.00 so the brightening pass is not active; vcache is off by default on this device; occlusion culling reports draws_skipped=0.00; pipeline eviction reports pipelines_new=0 evicted=0
moon_flicker_root_cause.key_finding_6: the draws counter is the GUEST draw-command count, not an engine re-issue count: the trace hook is reached from exactly one call site, the OP_DRAW_IDX case in execute() (xbg_game.cpp:5844), and every one of the 343205 traced lines is tagged cpu (gpu_draw_indexed returned false for all of them, so no draw was submitted twice by the engine). Therefore the guest program itself emits one extra draw-indexed command for the halo shader pair on 2 of every 6 frames.
moon_flicker_root_cause.key_finding_7: the guest time base is real time (nso_host.c uses clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) for the steady clock and the timer HLE), yet the 6-frame period does not stretch at 60 FPS (production CSV period-6 match 97.9 percent at 59.77 FPS). A guest that timed the effect from real time would have shown 12 frames at 60 FPS. So the periodicity is produced by frame-count-keyed state in the port, not by the game clock.
moon_flicker_root_cause.historical_link: the previously rejected commit 7b733b9 added xbg_writeback_is_current_slot() to find_indirect_template(); its own comment states the exact symptom: "Serving that older template draws with a stale instance count, which shows as a halo that alternates between two states frame by frame." That guard was dropped because it cost 2-3x frame rate, and the rescue baseline 5f4e2b5 does not contain it. The stale-writeback / slot-lifetime family is therefore the prime suspect for the extra draw, but it is not yet proven for this draw.
moon_flicker_root_cause.key_finding_4b: title screen shows no 6-frame period (40 draws per frame, each phase 91 percent identical), so the period is scene-specific and not injected globally by the engine; no frame-counter modulo 6 exists in the engine source
moon_flicker_root_cause.key_finding_8: the extra halo batch is a count=54 draw (54 indices = 9 quads) taken from a FIXED index buffer (guest address 0x6da0af0000) that is the same in every frame it appears in, while the base halo chain (11-12 draws) comes from a per-frame rotating index buffer. Four count-sequence shapes occur: 11 (no extra), 12 (one extra leading 54), 12 and 14 (two extra leading 54s). The leading extra appears in exactly 2 of every 6 phases.
moon_flicker_root_cause.key_finding_9: the cadence does not track anything the engine controls: gfx-slot-count 16, 8, 4 and 2 all reproduce the same period 6 (98.0-98.7 percent match), and 30 FPS and 60 FPS both reproduce period 6. It is therefore not the engine pipeline depth, not the frame pacing, and not a time-driven game tick.
moon_flicker_root_cause.key_finding_10: the counter/timestamp path is healthy: every REPORT request is matched by a publish, the publish latency is 0 or 1 frame (histogram 7975x1 frame + 5938x0 frames), and the published timestamp scale is correct (Vulkan timestampPeriod is 52.083332 ns per tick and the engine multiplies by 12/625, which is exactly 1 ns per tick). There is no stale-report or wrong-unit defect on that path.
moon_flicker_root_cause.key_finding_11: NOT a v1.0.6 regression: FFRS-v1.0.4.apk (published, package org.ffrs.gamewindow, versionCode 4) was installed over production with the same package name, so it ran against the same save directory, and its frame metrics reproduce the same period-6 cadence (dense segment period-6 match 100.0 percent, pattern 80,82,82,80,80,80). Caveat: the v1.0.4 automation stopped on the LOAD DATA dialog, so that dense segment is the menu background scene, not the moon scene proper.
moon_flicker_root_cause.external_reference: the original Nintendo Switch release of Final Fantasy Resonance targets 30 FPS; the native Switch 2 edition targets 60 FPS (SwitchRank review of the Switch release). At 30 FPS the port therefore reproduces the original cadence.
moon_flicker_root_cause.fps_conclusion: 60 FPS is technically reachable in the moon scene (59.77 FPS measured) but must not be shipped as the default: the halo cadence is frame-count driven, so doubling the frame rate halves the effect period from 200 ms to 100 ms and changes the game animation speed, which the task rules forbid; the dense crystal room also cannot hold 60 (gpu_ms 27.7 against a 16.67 ms budget, 22-23 FPS actual). Target stays 30 FPS unless the guest logic time base is made real-time, which is a separate change.
moon_flicker_root_cause.scene_identification_correction: CORRECTION 2026-11-12 (important): every 6-frame measurement in this task was taken on the LOAD DATA menu background rendering (about 80 draws per frame), not inside the game scene. The blind tap sequence used earlier often left the game on that menu, and the menu background has the same shader pair with the same 6-frame cadence. In the real scene (the 土之神殿 ruins reached with a verified cursor move to Yes) the per-frame draw count is about 755-773 and varies without any period (period-6 match about 7 percent, i.e. noise). Consequence: the four-switch A/B and the 30/60 FPS comparison falsify the menu cadence, not the moon flicker.
moon_flicker_root_cause.fps_sampling_correction: the screenrecord rate follows the application frame rate, so it is alias free for this workload: a 15 FPS run produced a 15.04 fps video (241 frames over 16.02 s, one video frame per game frame) and the earlier 30 FPS evidence video was about 32.75 fps. The earlier conclusion that the tablet screenrecord only samples at about 19.7 fps and therefore aliases a 30 FPS game was wrong and is withdrawn.
moon_flicker_root_cause.pixel_evidence_15fps: alias-free 15 FPS capture of the real scene (16 s, 241 frames): a 48x48 block periodicity map over the whole frame shows the strongest sustained per-frame change is the bottom-right fire (continuous animation); several small blocks alternate with period 2 (the sparkle motes); the purple halo region near (1100, 285) shows a slow pulse of about 18-20 frames and no 6-frame component; a static control region (stone path) shows the same period-2 component, so period 2 is a capture/display artefact rather than a game effect. Correlation between the per-frame draw count and the brightness of the most changing block is -0.03, i.e. none.

honor_moon_halo_20261112.scene: Load Data -> 01 -> Yes, one character save (01 战场 Lv.1 / Time 0:24), 3000x1920 device
honor_moon_halo_20261112.symptom: The moon halo alternates between two states. The wide soft halo around the moon switches on and off; the moon disc itself is pixel identical in both states, and the difference is a concentric ring peaking at r=50..60 px with an amplitude of 81 grey levels.
honor_moon_halo_20261112.not_a_fix: The appearance reported as 'the moon looks normal' is the state where the halo is completely absent (ROI 147.3..147.6), which is what the guest memory draw path renders. It is not a repair, it is the missing halo.
honor_moon_halo_20261112.engine_state_is_constant: Every field the engine records per draw is constant from frame to frame in that scene: index words, vertex buffer address and content hash, uniform address/size/content hash, texture handle and texture content signature, blend enable and factors, depth state, colour write mask, viewport, render target serial (the only change is the offscreen target ping-pong between serials 231 and 232), and the per frame draw and dispatch and submission counters.
honor_moon_halo_20261112.indirect_arguments_are_constant: The per frame probe (indirect-probe.csv, marker gfx-indirect-probe) shows all six indirect shader pairs keep their draw count, index count, instance count and first index constant over 300 frames.
honor_moon_halo_20261112.source_of_the_difference: The halo exists only on the GPU resident indirect path. The two paths that give the draw its arguments from guest memory (gfx-indexed-resident=0, and the current-slot guard in 7b733b9) both render the moon stable and without the halo.

conclusions: 30 FPS is reachable in the 01 scene: with a warm pipeline cache the same scene, save and package held 30.00 FPS for 150 s plus 242 s with max 34.59 ms and zero long frames. The stutter is a cold load cost, not a steady state defect.

The cold load long frames are concentrated in the first 7 seconds after entering the scene. The four worst are 1408.55 ms, 1156.70 ms, 862.46 ms and 641.57 ms, and the two worst have almost no draws (2 and 12) while taking over a second, which points at the synchronous disk read, SPIR-V rewrite and vkCreateShaderModule on the submit thread. This matches the static audit entry xbg_game.cpp:2501-2533 (shader_reuse=0). Static audit and device measurement corroborate each other here.

Backgrounding and returning to the foreground are the worst stutter source in this run: 8.60 FPS while backgrounded, p95 130 to 146 ms after returning, 80 to 113 frames above 100 ms per return, and present_result is 1 on every one of those long frames while normal frames are always 0. That is the surface rebuild path, where static audit P0-3 (vkDeviceWaitIdle without timeout) and P0-6 (ANativeWindow double lock race) live. Root cause not identified, so no fix is proposed.

save_storage.live_save_root: /storage/emulated/0/Android/data/org.ffrs.gamewindow/files/codex-local-save (confirmed by live_save_root log lines from 4 process starts during the soak)
save_storage.safe_from_update: External app specific storage. install -r keeps it, and neither force-stop nor install -r deletes it. A manual copy also exists at /sdcard/saves-bak-107.
save_storage.real_loss_mechanism: The guest only writes the save file at its own save points. GameSaveData0 stayed at its 13:38 mtime through a 22 minute session that included 4 force-stops, so progress since the last in game save point is lost whenever the process is killed, and installing an APK kills the process. The file is not deleted; the un-flushed progress is gone.
save_storage.secondary_1_restore_overwrites: onStop exports a snapshot to /sdcard/Download/FFRS-save-<timestamp>/ on every exit; 36 snapshots exist. Restoring an older one overwrites the live save root, so an old restore reads as lost progress.
save_storage.secondary_2_root_switch: GameActivity.java:2624-2627 switches the save root to getFilesDir()/saves when the data installer is in managed mode. This device is unmanaged (the internal directory does not exist), so it is not active now, but it is a real way for an update to make the save appear lost.
save_storage.secondary_3_isolated_flag: The isolated_regression_save intent extra can redirect the save root, but no such extra was used in this run.
save_storage.workaround_now: Trigger an in game save before updating, restore only the newest snapshot, and never wipe /sdcard/Android/data/org.ffrs.gamewindow/.

honor_stall_baseline_20261112.root_cause: CORRECTED. The stalls are NOT the synchronous creation of the effect pipelines. The live session reported pipelines_new=0 created=0 create_ms=0.0 create_max_ms=0.0, and the slowest synchronous creation ever measured was 127.0 ms, while the worst stall is 6506 ms. The engine also reported warm_built=1560 warm_failed=0 warm_ms=7010 warm_hits=0, so the seed was loaded and enabled (warm list seeded from /storage/emulated/0/FFRS/pipeline-warm-list.bin ok=1, warm list=1560 enabled=1) and the background thread built all 1560 pipelines in 7.01 s, yet not one of them was ever used. The working hypothesis is that the prewarm competes with the main thread for the driver and blocks it for seconds, and that the 1560 prebuilt pipelines are all useless because the bytes used as the lookup key never match the runtime request. The first 60 frame window reports wall_ms=9351.2, which is consistent with the 7010 ms prewarm cost.

honor_transition_real_rootcause_20261112.conclusion: The stall is not the prewarm and not defer_events. rg477m_texel_formatless_fatal_20261112.severity: blocking for the handheld: the game cannot be played at all, which outranks the stutter
rg477m_texel_formatless_fatal_20261112.symptom: the guest dies after about four to five seconds and about five presents with FATAL: Texel format lacks formatless-write support, and engine.log.fatal is written
rg477m_texel_formatless_fatal_20261112.pre_existing: the RG477M 1.0.8 engine.log ends with the same two lines, so this defect predates every change of this round
rg477m_texel_formatless_fatal_20261112.mechanism: the engine checks the per format buffer features of the texel format and requires VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_2_STORAGE_WRITE_WITHOUT_FORMAT when the binding asks for a formatless write. The check is at xbg_game.cpp:3834-3839 and the feature query at :2670-2683. The logic is correct: with format_feature_flags2=1 it uses the 64 bit VkFormatProperties3::bufferFeatures and prints it with %#llx, so there is no 32 bit truncation.

adreno_versus_mali.reading: the low 32 bits are the same on both, and the difference is only the high bits: 0x100000000 is VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_2_STORAGE_WRITE_WITHOUT_FORMAT_BIT and 0x80000000 is the read counterpart. Adreno reports both for every format it uses, Mali reports neither, so this is a whole device family difference rather than a single format.
adreno_versus_mali.spec: the Khronos VkFormatFeatureFlagBits2 specification states the two values and treats them as optional features, so an application must fall back to a typed path when they are missing

rg477m_texel_formatless_fatal_20261112.promising_path: the Mali flags 0x78 contain VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_2_STORAGE_TEXEL_BUFFER_BIT, so the typed storage texel buffer path is available. The candidate fix is to rewrite the SPIR-V so the formatless storage texel buffer access becomes a typed one, for example R32_UINT or R16_UINT, or a storage buffer with manual indexing. The project already has that machinery in xbg_spirv_indirect_instances.h, xbg_spirv_integer_buffer.h and xbg_spirv_stencil.h.

verdict.not_the_cause: synchronous pipeline creation. The largest single creation in the whole measured session is 1.3 ms; a slow window has 17 creations costing 6.8 ms in total.

verdict.ordering: neither causes the other. They are two independent costs of the same kind of frame and both land while the submit path is slow. The repair point is the drain scheduling.
verdict.cold_start: the 4.5-4.8 s cold-start frame is present with the warm-up on (4800 ms), off (4690 ms) and with no cache at all (4489 ms). It is scene and resource load, not the graphics path, and it is still unexplained.

rg477m_passprof_window_20261113.root_cause: A gfx-pass-profile marker left on the device set pass_prof_enabled for the whole session. indirect_dispatch_inputs_resident() and indexed_graphics_ready() both read that flag, so the GPU-resident indirect argument path was permanently off. Every frame then read the compute dispatch arguments on the CPU; the read overlapped a pending writeback range and resolve_pending() drained all 16 slots (fence ~46 ms/frame, sync_wb 2/frame). The CPU read the arguments before the GPU had written them (cpu_zero=1), so the compute dispatch was skipped entirely.
rg477m_passprof_window_20261113.fix: pass_prof_active() gates the two fast paths on the frame actually being sampled, not on a session-long flag. Startup banner now prints the pass profiler state.

The strip therefore replaced the game's depth with the rasterizer's interpolated z, and the LEQUAL comparison flipped along the contours of the depth difference, rejecting whole horizontal bands of the protagonist.
evidence: probe color0 at the protagonist draw: the figure is rasterized as 1 pixel high horizontal scanlines; the gaps are exactly (0,0,0,0) (3876 pixels, one single value) -> never written, not 'painted black'
offline SPIR-V: 0 OpLoad from the gl_FragCoord variable; gl_FragDepth is stored from a computed local value
A/B pair, same position, same APK, one boolean: strip on -> stripes present (8 alternating row pairs in the engine-side metric, 3 frames consistent); strip off -> stripes absent (0 row pairs)
the fix keeps the store for this shader, so the protagonist is solid; fps 30.00, submit_cpu_ms 2.55, sync_wb=0, sync_rb=0
